subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API config-write veto hook, and what ordering, trust, redaction, timeout, recursion, and failure semantics should it have across RPC and shared config mutation paths?
rationale: This would create a new plugin-facing security boundary around persisted configuration writes, so source inspection can prove the missing seam but cannot choose the acceptable trust and fail-closed policy.

options.title: Design guarded config-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow documented pre-persistence hook covering `config.set`, `config.patch`, `config.apply`, and shared mutation helpers with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, and rejection semantics.

options.title: Keep built-in validation only
options.body: Continue relying on core validation, SecretRef preflight, and agent-write allowlists, while documenting external validators as optional helpers that cannot enforce mandatory pre-apply policy.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight RFC
options.body: Defer this specific hook until the broader config validation/preflight direction chooses one shared validation contract.

recommendation.title: Design guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow documented pre-persistence hook covering `config.set`, `config.patch`, `config.apply`, and shared mutation helpers with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, and rejection semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this issue as an unresolved config validation/mutation boundary and have recent adjacent config-write history.
